source_text: Τί δὲ καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησε. παραστησάτω καὶ ἀποδειξάτω ὁ Κέλσος. ἀλλ᾿ οὐ δυνήσεται, μάλιστα ἐπεὶ εἴτ᾿ ἐκ παρακουσμάτων εἴτε καὶ ἐξ ἀναγνωσμάτων εὐαγγελικῶν εἴτ᾿ ἐκ διηγημάτων Ἰουδαϊκῶν οἴεται φέρειν ἃ λέγει κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἢ καθ᾿ ἡμῶν. ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ πάλιν ὁ Ἰουδαῖός φησιν ὅτι καὶ ἐλέγξαντες αὐτὸν καὶ καταγνόντες ἠξιοῦμεν κολάζεσθαι. δεικνύτωσαν, πῶς αὐτὸν ἤλεγξαν οἱ ζητοῦντες ψευδομαρτυρίας κατασκευάσαι αὐτῷ· εἰ μὴ ἄρα ὁ μέγας ἔλεγχος κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἦν. ὃν εἶπον οἱ κατήγοροι, ὅτι „οὗτος ἔφη· δύναμαι καταλῦσαι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἀναστῆσαι“· ἐπεὶ αὐτὸς μὲν „ἔλεγε περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ.“ ἐκεῖνοι δ᾿ ᾤοντο ὡς μὴ εἰδότες ἀκούειν κατὰ τὸ βούλημα τοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι περὶ τοῦ λιθίνου αὐτῷ ναοῦ ὁ λόγος ἦν, τοῦ τετιμημένου παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις μᾶλλον. ἢ ὡς ἐχρῆν τιμᾶσθαι τὸν ὡς ἀληθῶς ναὸν θεοῦ τοῦ λόγου καὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας. λεγέτω δέ τις, πῶς ἐπονειδιστότατα κρυπτόμενος διεδίδρασκεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· τὸ γὰρ ὀνείδους ἄξιόν τις παραστησάτω. ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεί φησι καὶ ὅτι ἑάλω. εἴποιμ᾿ ἂν ὅτι, εἴπερ τὸ ἁλῶναι ἀκούσιόν ἐστιν, οὐχ ἑάλω ὁ Ἰησοῦς· ἑαυτὸν γὰρ ἐν ἐπιτηδείῳ καιρῷ εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων γενέσθαι οὐκ ἐκώλυσεν ὡς „ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ,“ ἵν᾿ ἄρῃ „τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου.“ „εἰδὼς γοῦν πάντα τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸν ἐξῆλθε καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· τίνα ζητεῖτε; οἱ δ᾿ ἀπεκρίθησαν· Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον. λέγει δὲ αὐτοῖς· ἐγώ εἰμι. εἱστήκει δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν μετ᾿ αὐτῶν. ὡς οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· ἐγώ εἰμι, ἀπῆλθον εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ ἔπεσον χαμαί. πάλιν οὖν αὐτὸς ἐπηρώτησε· τίνα ζητεῖτε; οἱ δὲ εἶπον πάλιν· Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον. ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· εἶπον ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι· εἰ οὖν ἐμὲ ζητεῖτε, ἄφετε τούτους ὑπάγειν.‘· ἀλλὰ καὶ πρὸς τὸν βουλόμενον αὐτῷ βοηθῆσαι καὶ πατάξαντα „τὸν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως δοῦλον“ καὶ ἀφελόντα „αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτίον“ εἶπεν· „ἀπόστρεψον τὴν μάχαιράν σου εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς· πάντες γὰρ οἱ λαβόντες μάχαιραν ἐν μαχαίρᾳ ἀπολοῦνται. ἢ δοκεῖ σοι ὅτι οὐ δύναμαι ἄρτι παρακαλέσαι τὸν πατέρα μου, καὶ παραστήσει μοι ὧδε πλείους ἢ δώδεκα λεγεῶνας ἀγγέλων: πῶς οὖν πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ, ὅτι οὕτως ἔδει γενέσθαι;“ εἰ δὲ πλάσματα τῶν γραψάντων τὰ εὐαγγέλια οἴεταί τις εἶναι κατὰ ταῦτα, πῶς οὐχὶ μᾶλλον πλάσματα μέν ἐστι τὰ τῶν ἀπὸ ἔχθους καὶ μίσους τοῦ πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ Χριστιανοὺς λεγόντων, ἀλήθεια δὲ (τὰ) τῶν τὸ γνήσιον τῆς πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν διαθέσεως ἀποδειξαμένων ἐν τῷ πᾶν ὅ τι ποτ᾿ οὖν ὑπομεμενηκέναι διὰ τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ; τοσαύτην γὰρ ὑπομονὴν καὶ ἔνστασιν μέχρι θανάτου ἀνειληφέναι τοὺς Ἰησοῦ μαθητὰς μετὰ διαθέσεως ἀναπλασσούσης περὶ τοῦ διδασκάλου τὰ μὴ ὄντα . . . . . ; καὶ πολὺ τοῖς εὐγνωμονοῦσι τὸ ἐναργές ἐστι περὶ τοῦ πεπεῖσθαι αὐτοὺς περὶ ὧν ἀνέγραψαν ἐκ τοῦ τηλικαῦτα καὶ τοσαῦτα διὰ τὸν πεπιστευμένον αὐτοῖς εἶναι υἱὸν θεοῦ ὑπομεμενηκέναι.
pass_a_gloss: What did Jesus promise (ἐπαγγέλλομαι) and not do (ποιέω)? Let Celsus present (παρίστημι) and demonstrate (ἀποδείκνυμι). But he will not be able, especially since he supposes (οἴομαι) he brings what he says against Jesus or against us either from mishearings (παράκουσμα) or from Gospel readings (ἀνάγνωσμα εὐαγγελικόν) or from Jewish narratives (διήγημα Ἰουδαϊκόν). But since again the Jew says that 'having convicted (ἐλέγχω) him and condemned (καταγιγνώσκω) him we deemed (ἀξιόω) him to be punished (κολάζω)', let them show how those seeking to fabricate (κατασκευάζω) false testimonies (ψευδομαρτυρία) against him convicted him; unless the great proof/conviction (ἔλεγχος) against Jesus was what the accusers (κατήγορος) said: 'this man said: I am able to destroy (καταλύω) the temple (ναός) of God and through three days raise it (ἀνίστημι)'; since he himself spoke about the temple of his body (σῶμα), while they supposed, as not knowing how to hear according to the intention (βούλημα) of the speaker, that his word was about the stone (λίθινος) temple, the one honoured (τιμάω) among the Jews rather than, as was needed (χρή), the truly (ἀληθῶς) temple of God the Word (λόγος) and of Wisdom (σοφία) and of Truth (ἀλήθεια) being honoured. Let someone say how Jesus, hiding (κρύπτομαι), slipped away (διαδιδράσκω) most disgracefully (ἐπονειδιστότατα); let someone present what was worthy of reproach (ὄνειδος). But since he says also that he was caught (ἁλίσκομαι), I would say that, if being caught is involuntary (ἀκούσιος), Jesus was not caught; for at a fitting time (ἐπιτήδειος καιρός) he did not prevent (κωλύω) himself coming into hands of men, as 'lamb (ἀμνός) of God', that he might take away (αἴρω) 'the sin of the world'. 'Knowing (οἶδα) then all things coming upon him he went out and says to them: whom do you seek? They answered: Jesus the Nazorean. He says: I am. Judas who betrays him stood with them. When he said I am, they went back and fell to the ground. Again he asked: whom do you seek? They said again: Jesus the Nazorean. Jesus answered: I told you that I am; if then you seek me, let these go away (ἀφίημι ὑπάγειν).' But also to the one wishing to help (βοηθέω) him and having struck (πατάσσω) the high priest's slave (δοῦλος) and taken off (ἀφαιρέω) his ear (ὠτίον) he said: 'turn back (ἀποστρέφω) your sword (μάχαιρα) to its place; for all who take the sword will perish (ἀπόλλυμι) by the sword. Or does it seem to you that I cannot now summon (παρακαλέω) my Father, and he will set beside (παρίστημι) me here more than twelve legions (λεγεών) of angels? How then would the Scriptures (γραφαί) be fulfilled (πληρόω), that thus it must (δεῖ) happen?' If someone supposes these are fictions (πλάσμα) of those who wrote the Gospels in these respects, how are not rather fictions those of the ones speaking from enmity (ἔχθος) and hatred (μῖσος) toward him and Christians, and truth those of the ones who showed the genuineness (τὸ γνήσιον) of their disposition (διάθεσις) toward Jesus in having endured (ὑπομένω) anything whatever for his words? For that the disciples of Jesus took up such endurance (ὑπομονή) and resistance/steadfastness (ἔνστασις) until death with a disposition fabricating (ἀναπλάσσω) about the teacher things that are not . . . [lacuna]; and much is the evidence (τὸ ἐναργές) to the fair-minded (εὐγνωμονέω) about their being persuaded (πείθομαι) of what they recorded (ἀναγράφω), from their having endured such great and so many things for the one believed by them to be Son of God.
pass_b_english: But what did Jesus promise and not do? Let Celsus set it out and prove it. He will not be able to, above all because what he says against Jesus, or against us, he supposes he draws either from things misheard, or from readings of the Gospels, or from Jewish stories.

Again, since the Jew says that “we convicted him, condemned him, and judged that he should be punished,” let them show how those who were seeking to contrive false testimony against him convicted him (Matthew 26:59–60); unless, perhaps, the great proof against Jesus was the one his accusers stated: “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and to raise it up in three days’” (Matthew 26:61). For he himself “was speaking of the temple of his body” (John 2:21), while they, not knowing how to hear according to the speaker’s intention, thought that he meant the temple of stone, which the Jews honoured rather than honouring, as was right, the true temple of God the Word, of Wisdom and of Truth.

Let someone also tell us how Jesus “hid himself and slipped away most shamefully.” Let someone point out what in this deserved reproach. And since he says that he was also “caught,” I would reply that if being caught means being taken against one’s will, Jesus was not caught. For at the fitting time he did not prevent himself from coming into the hands of men, as “the Lamb of God,” so that he might take away “the sin of the world” (John 1:29). Indeed, “knowing all that was coming upon him, he went out and said to them, ‘Whom are you seeking?’ They answered, ‘Jesus of Nazareth.’ He said to them, ‘I am he.’ Judas also, who was betraying him, was standing with them. When he said to them, ‘I am he,’ they drew back and fell to the ground. So he asked again, ‘Whom are you seeking?’ And they said again, ‘Jesus of Nazareth.’ Jesus answered them, ‘I told you that I am he. So if you are seeking me, let these men go’” (John 18:4–8). Moreover, to the one who wanted to help him, who struck “the servant of the high priest” and cut off “his ear” (Matthew 26:51), he said: “Put your sword back into its place; for all who take the sword will perish by the sword. Or do you think that I cannot now call on my Father, and he will set beside me here more than twelve legions of angels? How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?” (Matthew 26:52–54).

If anyone thinks that in these matters the accounts are fictions made up by those who wrote the Gospels, why are the words of those who speak out of enmity and hatred toward him and toward Christians not rather the fictions, and the accounts of those who proved the sincerity of their devotion to Jesus by enduring anything whatever for the sake of his words the truth? For that the disciples of Jesus should have taken on such endurance and steadfastness, even to death, while their minds were inventing about their teacher things that never were […]. And to fair-minded people it is abundantly clear that they were persuaded of what they recorded, from the fact that they endured such great and so many sufferings for the sake of the one they believed to be the Son of God.

choices.why: οἴεται φέρειν: 'thinks he can draw' had added 'can'; now 'he supposes he draws', with εἴτε ... εἴτε kept as 'either ... or'
πῶς αὐτὸν ἤλεγξαν οἱ ζητοῦντες: passive 'he was convicted by men' made active to match the Greek agency; the 'Unless' fragment joined to its sentence
John 18:5, 18:7: removed 'him' and 'them', which Origen's text lacks; added 'also' for καί (Judas also was standing with them)
κατὰ ταῦτα clause made plainer ('in these matters the accounts are fictions')
translator note on Matthew 26:53 corrected: Origen moves ἄρτι and adds ὧδε, he does not replace one with the other

checked: Matthew 26:59-61, John 2:21, John 1:29, John 18:4-8, Matthew 26:51-54 all match the clauses they sit beside; Celsus's Jew's words ('we convicted him ...', 'hid himself and slipped away most shamefully', 'caught') match 2.9 and stay in quotation marks; lacuna kept, not filled

translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau marks a lacuna after τὰ μὴ ὄντα (printed as dots); the main clause that should follow (presumably something like ‘is not credible’) is lost, and it is left as [lacuna] rather than supplied. The Jew’s words in paragraph two repeat his charge from 2.9 (ἐλέγξαντες αὐτὸν καὶ καταγνόντες ἠξιοῦμεν κολάζεσθαι), so they are quoted; likewise “hid himself and slipped away most shamefully” (κρυπτόμενος ... διαδιδράσκων ἐπονειδιστότατα) and “caught” (ἑάλω). Matthew 26:61: Origen’s text has ἀναστῆσαι (‘raise up’) where Matthew reads οἰκοδομῆσαι (‘build’), perhaps under the influence of John 2:19–21 (ἐγερῶ); translated as Origen wrote it. Matthew 26:53: Origen puts ἄρτι (‘now’) before παρακαλέσαι and adds ὧδε (‘here’) after παραστήσει μοι; both kept. John 18:5, 18:7: Origen’s text lacks αὐτῷ / αὐτούς (‘him’, ‘them’), so they are not supplied. ‘The temple of God the Word, of Wisdom and of Truth’ (ναὸν θεοῦ τοῦ λόγου καὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας): the genitives could also be taken as ‘the temple of God, of the Word, of Wisdom and of Truth’; the sense (Jesus’ body as the true temple of the divine Word) is the same. The construction μᾶλλον ἢ ὡς ἐχρῆν τιμᾶσθαι is read as ‘rather than, as was right, the true temple being honoured’. ‘Coming into the hands of men’ (εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων) may echo Matthew 17:22 / Mark 9:31; possible allusion only, not cited inline. ‘Jesus of Nazareth’ renders Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον.
